chunks: Certainly this world is a place of passage, and the Hereafter is a place of permanent abode. So, take from your passage for your permanent abode, and do not tear away your curtain before Him Who knows your secrets. Take your hearts out of this world before your bodies go out of it, for herein you have been put on trial, and you have been created for the other world.
When a man dies, people ask: 'What has he left?' and the angels ask: 'What has he sent forward?'
May Allah bless you; send forward something, it will be a loan for you, and do not leave everything behind, for that would be a burden on you.

key_terms.أَسْتَارَكُمْ: Your veils or curtains, referring to one's inner state or secrets
key_terms.الآخِرَةُ: The Hereafter, the eternal life to come
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life, the present temporal existence
key_terms.دَارُ قَرَارٍ: A place of permanent abode or settlement
key_terms.دَارُ مَجَازٍ: A place of passage or transit
key_terms.قَرْضاً: A loan, referring to good deeds that yield return

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the world as a passage and the Hereafter as a permanent abode according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of the world as a 'passing station' (dar al-majaz) to urge believers to purify their hearts before death, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology regarding the transition from the temporal to the eternal. This sermon highlights the contrast between human concern for material inheritance and the angelic record of spiritual deeds, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on *amal* (deeds) as a loan to the Hereafter. It serves as a practical guide for self-accountability (*muhasaba*) before the final departure from this testing ground.

en.sayed-ali-raza: certainly this world is a passage while the next world is a place of permanent abode. So, take from the passage (all that you can) for the permanent abode. Do not tear away your curtain before Him Who is aware of your secrets. Take away from this world your hearts before your bodies go out of it, because herein you have been put on trial, and you have been created for the other world.
When a man dies people ask what (property) he has left while the angels ask what (good actions) he has sent forward.
May Allāh bless you; send forward something, it will be a loan for you, and do not leave everything behind, for that would be a burden on you.
